issues.description: Malformed-row threshold is checked after committed upserts, so a failed ingest can still persist partial data.
Timestamp filters and max-window logic compare raw ISO strings lexicographically, producing wrong results for date-only or offset timestamps.
Timestamps are validated but returned unnormalized, allowing inconsistent date-only, naive, and timezone-aware values into storage.
GPU TRES parsing matches any key starting with gres/gpu, so gres/gpumem and gres/gpuutil are treated as GPU counts or hard failures.
Failure-state detection omits Slurm OUT_OF_MEMORY, so documented out-of-memory failures are excluded from failure reports.
Rows with extra pipe-delimited columns are silently accepted because DictReader's None overflow field is ignored.
Ingest only catches RowParseError, so decode, permission, and SQLite errors can crash with a traceback instead of a CLI error.
All report paths create and initialize a database, so a typo in --db silently reports against a new empty DB.
The parser loads every valid job into memory before writing, which will scale poorly for large sacct exports.
